The bug: `dayKey` uses local-time getters but is documented (and tested) to group by **UTC** calendar day. With `TZ=America/New_York`, `2026-01-02T02:30:00Z` is Jan 1 locally, so it returns `"2026-01-01"`. Let me check other usages before fixing.

3 tests fail — I need to see which ones, since I must only fix the timezone cause and keep everything else green.

Two other tests also fail (`[cli-flag]` and `[null-guard]`). Let me inspect them and their sources to understand the full picture.

Let me check the remaining tests, README, and any prior session context to understand scope.

The README settles the scope question: **"Three tests fail on purpose: `cli-flag`, `null-guard` and `timezone`."** So `cli-flag` and `null-guard` are separate, deliberately-broken tasks — I must not touch them. My job: fix the root cause of the `timezone` failure only, and keep the 6 currently-green tests green.

**Root cause:** the comment in `dates.js` says day keys group by calendar day **in UTC**, but the code uses local-time getters (`getFullYear`/`getMonth`/`getDate`). Under `TZ=America/New_York`, `2026-01-02T02:30:00Z` falls on Jan 1 local time, producing `"2026-01-01"`. The fix is in the production code (UTC getters), not the test.

Now verify: timezone passes, the previously-green tests stay green, and the two intentional failures are untouched.

Quick sanity check that `dayKey` is now timezone-independent (and confirm `git diff` shows the minimal change):

Fixed. 

**Root cause:** `dayKey` in `packages/shared/src/dates.js` was documented to group events by calendar day **in UTC**, but used local-time getters (`getFullYear`/`getMonth`/`getDate`). With `TZ=America/New_York`, the UTC instant `2026-01-02T02:30:00Z` falls on Jan 1 local time, so it returned `"2026-01-01"` instead of `"2026-01-02"`.

**Fix** (production code, not the test): swapped to the UTC equivalents — `getUTCFullYear()`/`getUTCMonth()`/`getUTCDate()`.

**Verification:**
- `[timezone] day keys are UTC days` ✅ passes
- All 6 previously-green tests ✅ still pass
- Output is now identical under `UTC`, `America/New_York`, `Asia/Tokyo`, and `Pacific/Kiritimati` (+14)
- `dayKey` has no other callers in the repo, so no downstream behavior changed

**Note on the two remaining failures:** `[cli-flag]` and `[null-guard]` still fail, but the README states these (along with `timezone`) "fail on purpose" — they're separate seeded bugs (`flags.js` leaving numbers as strings; `displayName` crashing on `null`). Since your ask was to fix the timezone cause only, I left them untouched; say the word if you want those fixed too.
